name: Medial Epicondylalgia (Golfer's Elbow)
summary: Load-related pain at the common flexor-pronator tendon origin, aggravated by gripping, wrist flexion or forearm pronation.

looksLike: Pain with gripping, lifting or throwing
Possible tingling in ring/little fingers if ulnar nerve involved
redFlags: Progressive ulnar nerve weakness or persistent sensory loss
Hot swollen joint, fever or fracture concern
firstSteps: Temporarily reduce high-irritability gripping and throwing volume

tests.name: Resisted Wrist Flexion and Pronation
tests.purpose: Reproduce tendon-related medial elbow symptoms under controlled load.
tests.positive: Familiar pain at common flexor origin.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Temporarily reduce high-irritability gripping and throwing volume
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.
do: Build grip and proximal shoulder capacity
Gradually restore occupational and sport-specific loading
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Progress high-speed throwing, lifting and sustained grip
dose: Progress resistance and task duration over weeks
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: Pain-tolerable grip strength near functional target

structures: Common flexor tendon, especially flexor-pronator origin
Ulnar nerve may be irritated in some cases
mechanism: Repeated gripping, throwing or wrist-flexion/pronation load
Abrupt increase in manual work or sport volume
classification: Consider associated ulnar neuropathy or ligament injury
investigations: Usually clinical; ultrasound/MRI only if diagnosis uncertain, significant tear or persistent symptoms.
Nerve studies/medical review when progressive neurological symptoms exist.
manual: Mobilization with movement may provide short-term relief in selected cases.
Manual therapy is adjunctive; progressive loading is central.
modalities: Counterforce strap or wrist support may help selected activities temporarily.
Avoid relying on ultrasound/electrotherapy as primary treatment.
mistakes: Missing ulnar neuropathy or UCL injury
Treating tenderness without restoring grip capacity
pearls: Medial elbow pain plus ring/little-finger paraesthesia should prompt ulnar nerve assessment.
Load tolerance, not pain on one test alone, guides progression.

tests.name: Resisted Wrist Flexion and Pronation
tests.purpose: Reproduce tendon-related medial elbow symptoms under controlled load.
tests.positive: Familiar pain at common flexor origin.
tests.patientPosition: Seated; elbow initially flexed, forearm supinated; resist wrist flexion and pronation separately.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: Supports flexor-pronator tendinopathy; assess ulnar nerve and UCL where indicated.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
